newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends lower, techs leap higher in mixed session.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends lower, techs leap higher in mixed session.

text.p: U.S. stocks finished broadly mixed on Tuesday, with blue chips limping to narrow losses but tech stocks extending their recent scorching gains.

The Dow industrials fell 11 points to close unofficially at 8188. Broader indexes were generally higher, however, and the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite finished with a one percent gain to post its third straight record high.
The session highlighted a recent trend of increasingly impatient investors showing a willingness to flock to and from groups based on any signs of shifting market psychology.

"This market has been marked by group and sector rotations in very short timeframes," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "With the primary market languishing, Nasdaq and the techs are pressing higher."

A main reason that blue chips have hit a wall is a run-up in interest rates after recent evidence economic growth may be accelerating, traders and analysts said. Rates edged higher again Tuesday, dragging on the performance of financial stocks.
"One disappointing area today was financial services, which continues to trade in lockstep with the yield curve," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
Among banks, Chase Manhattan Corp fell 1-7/16 to 109-9/16, and BankAmerica Corp shed 1-5/8 to 71-7/8.

The Dow's tepid results aside, the day belonged to tech stocks. Intel Corp rose 2-15/16 to 99-11/16 after briefly brushing past the 100-point mark, while Microsoft Corp rose 1-3/4 to 143-5/16 and disk drive maker Western Digital Corp added 5-3/8 to 45-1/2.
"The chip stocks were on fire, the software names were on fire and the disk drive makers were on fire," Orlando said.
Networking leader Cisco Systems Inc rose 5/16 to 81-15/16 ahead of the release of its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings.

After the close, Cisco reported its operating profit rose 34 percent, matching official Wall Street expectations. Even so, Cisco fell to 79-3/4 in after-hours trading, suggesting Wall Street's unofficial expectations may have run ahead of reality.

"The Cisco after-hours action shows there was a whiff of speculation in the activity today," Bleier said. "We're not deeply in the realm of speculative activity but we have certainly entered the outer halls."

Among individual issues, Aetna Inc tumbled 14-1/4 to 102-3/4 after the company reported weaker-than-expected second-quarter results. Smith Barney downgraded the shares, citing disappointment with Aetna's managed-care results.
Lone Star Steakhouse & Saloon Inc fell four points to 18 after warning its third-quarter results would fail to meet Wall Street estimates.
The S&P 500 index rose 2.07 points to 952.37.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 16.08 to a record 1621.53.
